DATED : 10/12 APRIL 2023 P.C. :-
1.

These three Contempt Petitions are filed by the Petitioners alleging willful disobedience of the order dated 13 th April 2022 passed by this Court in Writ Petition Nos. 3544 of 2020 and 3545 of 2020 and order dated 5th May 2022 passed in Writ Petition No. 5587 of 2021.

entities.text: Writ Petition Nos. 3544 of 2020 and 3545 of 2020
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: By these orders this Court allowed the above three Writ Petitions and was pleased to quash and set aside Government Resolution dated 15th July 2010 being violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India and has declared that the Respondent had no authority to deduct 10% from the amount of compensation payable to the Petitioners on account of compulsory acquisition.
This Court accordingly disposed of the Writ Petitions.
2. Petitioners thereafter addressed a letter on 25 th April 2022 to the Competent Authority followed by series of letters calling upon the Respondent to comply with the orders of this Court.

On 16 th June 3/8 908.563.22 cp.doc 2022, Sub-Divisional Officer and Competent Authority informed the Petitioners that the Respondents have sought guidance from the State Government on the issue of releasing the payment as claimed by the Petitioners.

3. We have also perused the correspondence addressed by the Sub-Divisional Officer and Competent Authority to the Collector, Palghar seeking guidance from the Diksha Dilip Pawar And Ors vs Swapnil Subhash Tangde, The Competent ...

2 Collector after referring to the order passed by this Court thereby quashing and setting aside the Government Resolution dated 15th July 2010 permitting deduction of 10% amount from the compensation.
4. We have perused the Affidavit-in-Reply filed by the Competent Authority in these two Contempt Petitions.

There was no time prescribed by this Court while allowing the Writ Petition filed by the Petitioners and quashing and setting aside the Government Resolution based on which 10% amount was deducted from the compensation payable to the Petitioners in respect of the land in question.

5. Mr. D'Souza, learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that there is no dispute that National Highway Authority of India has deposited the entire compensation amount with the Competent Authority in respect of the land in question, however,
the Competent 4/8 908.563.22 cp.doc Authority has deducted 10% amount based on the said Government Resolution which is already quashed and set aside by this Court.

6. Dr. Warunjikar, learned counsel for Respondent submitted that since there was no time prescribed in the order passed by this Court, while allowing the Writ Petitions filed by the Petitioner and quashing and setting the Government Resolution permitting such 10% deductions, there is no question of any contempt committed.
7. We have perused the correspondence exchanged between the parties since June 2022.
Even if there is no time prescribed in complying with the order passed by this Court, order passed by this Court has to be complied within a reasonable time.
Respondent Competent Authority did not bother to comply with the order within a reasonable time and on the contrary continues to seek opinion either from the State Government or from the Collector.
Respondent also did not seek any clarification from this Court about the timeline not prescribed by this Court while disposing the Writ Petitions filed by the Petitioners.

8. These matters were on board on 10 th April 2023 and after hearing learned counsel for the parties, this Court prima facie opined that Respondents have committed willful disobedience of the order passed by this Court on 13th April 2022/5th May,
2022 and directed 5/8 908.563.22 cp.doc the office to accordingly issue Show Cause Notice to the Respondent under the provisions of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 read with Article 2015 of the Constitution of India.
This Court also proposed to direct the Competent Authority to deposit the said amount in this Court within 48 hours without fail.

9. After the dictation of the order was over Dr Warunjikar learned counsel for the Respondent made a request that he will try to persuade the State Government to permit the Respondent to release the amount deducted and sought one day's time for this exercise.
The Court accepted the said request of the learned counsel and directed the office to place the matter on supplementary board on 12th April 2023.

sentences.text: 10. Dr Warunjikar learned counsel for the Respondent tendered copy of the Review Petition (St) No. 10459 of 2023 filed by his client in this Court inter alia praying for recall of the order dated 13 th April, 2022 /5th May, 2022 passed by the Division Bench of this Court in Civil Writ Petition Nos. 3544 of 2020, 3545 of 2020 and 5587 of 2021.

entities.text: Civil Writ Petition Nos. 3544 of 2020, 3545 of 2020 and 5587 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: We are informed by the learned counsel for the parties that by order passed by the Division Bench presided over by The Acting 6/8 908.563.22 cp.doc Chief Justice, the said Review Petition filed by the Respondent in the Contempt Petition has been rejected.

There is some dispute as to whether the Respondent in the Contempt Petition has been granted four weeks time in the Review Petition to comply with the order dated 13th April 2022/5th May 2022 by this Court or not.

11. Dr. Warunjikar learned counsel for the Respondent in the Contempt Petition submitted that after this Contempt Petition was heard by this Court on 10th April 2023 his client was advised by the State Government to file Review Petition in this Court.
We have perused the annexures to the Review Petition filed by the Respondent.

A perusal of the letter dated 1st March 2023 from the Desk Officer, State Government to the Collector, it was made clear that the reference to the two Government Resolutions dated 11 th January 2017 and 27th December 2018 were not brought to the notice of this Court, when the said order dated 13 th April 2022 was passed.

By the said letter dated 1st March 2023, general directions were issued to make a reference of the two Government Resolutions dated 11th January 2017 and 27 th December 2018, while releasing compensation amount.
Copy of the said communication was served upon the Respondent on 6th April 2023.
Averment in that regard is made in paragraph 5 of the Review Petition.

When the matter was 7/8 908.563.22 cp.doc argued on 10th April 2023 before this Court there was no reference to the said communication dated 1 st March 2023 from the Desk Officer of the State Government to the Collector.

12. Learned counsel for the Respondent vehemently urged that in view of the advise received by the said letter dated 1 st March 2023 that the Government Resolutions were not pointed out to this Court, when the said order dated 13th April 2022/5th May 2022 was passed, on the basis of such advise during interregnum period of two days, his client in his personal capacity filed Review Petition in this Court.
In our view, Respondent has not only misled this Court but also the bench presided over by the Hon'ble Acting Chief Justice in the Review Petition at this stage.
13. Learned counsel for the Respondent states that his client is ready and willing to comply with the order dated 13 th April 2022 by calling the parties to his office during the course of the day.
When the learned counsel was asked to make a statement whether payment will be released or not, he submitted that procedure for releasing payment, would be commenced today.

sentences.text: In our prima facie view, Respondent has committed willful disobedience of the order passed by this Court on 13 th April 2022/5th May 2022.

Office is accordingly directed to issue Show Cause Notice 8/8 908.563.22 cp.doc to the Respondent under the provisions of Contempt of Courts Act read with Article 215 of the Constitution of India to show cause as to why appropriate action should not be taken against Respondent for non compliance of the order dated 13 th April 2022/5th May 2022.
Notice is made returnable on 24th April 2023, to be placed high on board.

15. In view of the statement made by the learned counsel for the Respondent that his client is ready and willing to comply with the order passed by this Court, we direct the Respondent to deposit the entire amount in this Court within 48 hours without fail with intimation to the learned counsel for the Petitioner.
16. Stand over to 24th April 2023.
High on board.
